runs.name: Avista Corporation; NYSE AVA, SEC CIK 0000104918, Washington, 10-K filer, formerly Washington Water Power Co. until 1998; regulated electric and natural gas utility, two segments (Avista Utilities in Washington, Idaho, Oregon and Montana; AEL&P in Juneau, Alaska) plus Avista Capital investments; its 15 percent of Colstrip Units 3 and 4 transferred to NorthWestern 2026-01-01; Spokane-area wildfires from 2026-08-01 damaged its West Spokane transmission and distribution; no rename, merger, spin-off or split in the 8-Ks since the 10-K; the 10-K names no SEC-filing rival, IDACORP, Portland General and NorthWestern chosen as a CONVENTION of the run
runs.box: OUT AT Q7, ON THE FLOOR
runs.entry: Price **$36.67** (close 2026-10-16, printed by `tools/run.py` from an aggregator, flagged). Shares 83,752,830 at 2026-07-24 from the 10-Q cover (0001193125-26-329083), one class, no treasury stock; the sales-agency programme continues. Sovereign **5.43%**, the US Treasury 30-year par yield of 2026-10-16 (issuing authority). Read from the 10-K for 2025 (0001193125-26-067872), the Q1 and Q2 2026 10-Qs, the 2026 proxy (0001193125-26-138034), the FY2022 10-K (0000950170-23-003546) and the 8-Ks of 2026 including the Washington multi-year rate plan (0001193125-26-015443), the data-centre memorandum and its pause, and the Spokane wildfires (0001193125-26-329442); 2025 operating cash $469M checked to the filed statement. Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from Items 1, 1A and 7, stated in the run file. **Q1 IN**: rate base, allowed return and load set in public proceedings years ahead; wildfire sent to Q9. **Q2 IN as a regulated second best**: a natural-monopoly franchise, ordinary returns carried to Q3 under the regulator exception; Avista Utilities deciding at 93% of five-year net income; the 10-K names only non-filing cooperatives and public utility districts, IDACORP, Portland General and NorthWestern chosen as a CONVENTION of the run, Avista lowest or tied lowest on return on book equity in six of ten years 2016 to 2025 and below IDACORP in nine; a large industrial customer left in April 2026. **Q3 weighs against**: return on book equity 6.5% to 7.3% every year 2020 to 2025 against allowed 9.4% to 9.8%, about 5.9% on added equity, capital spending about twice depreciation, funded by debt and shares. **Q4 IN, weighs against mildly**: inventory rise explained by Note 3 (emission allowances); featured non-GAAP utility EPS, guidance, an unexplained proxy EPS of 2.76. **Q5 integrity IN, ability weighs against mildly.** **Q6 weighs against**: about 54 cents of market value per dollar retained or raised since 2016, shares sold every year ($78M in 2025, up to $90M planned for 2026) against $159M of dividends, long-term pay on cumulative EPS with no capital charge. **Q7 OUT on the floor and above the top of the range**: owner cash 2021 to 2025 $196.1M a year all-equity after maintenance (depreciation as the guess), $97.7M equity, -$138.5M after all spending, negative every year; net debt $3,335M at 2026-06-30; value range **$3.29 to $9.97 a share all-equity** (equity-only $8.54 to $21.48); expected return 3.1% to 4.8% at the price; fair price -$20.47 all-equity, not positive, $3.21 equity-only. Debt about $1.85B (2016) to $3.36B (2025), 54.4% of capital; retained earnings supplied $324M of a $1.06B equity rise; $141M of collateral called in 2022. Lapses declared by the analyst: Q5 and Q6 committed together; the Q7 arithmetic first computed and committed while Q1 to Q4 were open, without the COMPUTATION, NOT A CLEARANCE heading, added the next step (operator rule 3), numbers entering the run file only at Q7. Contamination declared by the analyst: a `Test Runs/` listing of fourteen other 2026-10-18 run names, AEP commit subjects, ARCB and AYI file names, the memory index; none used. Commits 09472e24 (template), 39b4f5db (Step 0, Q1), 0c1a5ec8 (Q2), 5e9982fc (Q3), 07a38fee (Q4), 3490d491 (Q5, Q6), 2c135295 (Q7, Q6 line written back), 9000b364 (box, after the stop, self-audit, gaps). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's `check_cites.py` 67 ids no problem; the dispatcher's `dispatcher_cites.py` no missing id, 47 adjacent quoted fragments, **no citation slip**. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator** (the analyst's framework notes): (1) Q2's regulator exception is silent on a utility that persistently earns well below its allowed return and its neighbours; (2) depreciation as the maintenance proxy against the row calling utility depreciation inadequate; (3) whether (e)'s growth spending scales with growth or stays flat ($9.97 against $21.07); (4) (b)'s halves of an odd-year window; (5) (f)'s sales growth inflated by pass-through commodity costs; (6) Whose tax silent on regulatory flow-through; (7) how to report or arm a negative all-equity fair price; (8) the named-rival rule at a regulated monopoly. Not armed: all-equity fair not positive, no organic-pair figure (no acquisitions). Could not get: capital spending by category (a graph), retail rates against neighbours, whether directors bought or were granted shares, the meaning of the proxy's 2.76 EPS.
runs.narr: OUT at Q7, on the floor and above the top of the range (Avista Corporation, NYSE AVA; regulated electric and gas distribution in Washington, Idaho, Oregon and Montana and AEL&P in Juneau; Q1 IN; Q2 IN as a regulated second best, Avista Utilities deciding at 93%; Q3 against, return on equity 6.5% to 7.3% against allowed 9.4% to 9.8%; Q4 IN, mildly against; Q5 integrity IN, ability mildly against; Q6 against, shares sold every year to fund the dividend; value range $3.29 to $9.97 all-equity at $36.67, expected return 3.1% to 4.8%, fair -$20.47 all-equity, not positive, $3.21 equity-only; no citation slip; not held; not armed; lapses declared: Q5 with Q6 committed together, Q7 arithmetic run early without the heading; framework gaps for the operator: the regulator exception for a chronic under-earner, utility depreciation as maintenance, (e)'s growth-spending level, (b)'s halves, (f) on pass-through sales, flow-through tax, a negative fair price, the named-rival rule)
